prompt.context: Nica Productions is an American Media company that is trying to figure out which will be its next project. This company has extensive experience producing series and movies for all types of audiences and has received many awards doing so. The company has two alternatives: produce a series for a streaming company or a movie to be projected in cinemas worldwide. Producing media content implies big investments and low certainty about potential income, which depends on many factors. For that reason, our client has hired us to help decide which is the best alternative.
prompt.question: Which project should Nica Productions choose — the movie or the series — and why?

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profitability goal?
clarifying_info.a: No, there is no specific profitability goal.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have access to top talent?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the company is worldwide known with access to top star directors, actors, and technical staff.
No, there is no budget limitation.

clarifying_info.q: What is the target audience for each alternative?
clarifying_info.a: Both alternatives seek worldwide reach but target different types of customers.
Production of either alternative will last one year.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any alternative project if neither is chosen?
clarifying_info.a: No, there is no alternative project.

clarifying_info.q: What is the main source of revenue for both projects?
clarifying_info.a: The main source of revenue for both projects depends on audience size.

exhibits.title: Movies Alternatives
exhibits.shows: Two movie director/cast alternatives with associated probabilities of attracting different audience sizes, plus cost breakdown by role for each alternative. Also shows the probability of selecting each alternative.
exhibits.data: Alternative 1 (Christopher Nolan, target: Teenagers and Young Adults, 60% probability of being chosen): 70% chance of 600M audience, 30% chance of 400M audience; Director 25M USD, Tom Hardy 50M USD, Michael Cain 25M USD, Production & Marketing 50M USD. Alternative 2 (Michael Bay, target: Kids and Teenagers, 40% probability of being chosen): 80% chance of 400M audience, 20% chance of 200M audience; Director 10M USD, Mark Wahlberg 25M USD, Tyrese Gibson 5M USD, Production & Marketing 60M USD. Note: Filmmakers receive 10% of ticket sales (10 USD/ticket).

exhibits.title: Series
exhibits.shows: Cost breakdown for the series alternative, additional data on upfront payment and episode details, and a probability table for audience per episode at three levels.
exhibits.data: Expenses: Script already bought 10M USD, Actors 60M USD, Production 40M USD. Upfront: 20M USD. Number of episodes: 10. Income per episode (PMV): 600,000 USD. Audience levels: High 100M per episode at 30%, Medium 70M per episode at 40%, Bad 40M per episode at 30%.

exhibits.title: Movie Alternative 2 — Merchandising and Other Income Cash Flows
exhibits.shows: A bar chart of annual cash flows (in M USD) from merchandising and other income streams for Movie Alternative 2, from year 0 through approximately year 11, showing a declining trend over time.
exhibits.data: Year 1: 20.00M, Year 2: 18.00M, Year 3: 16.20M, Year 4: 14.58M, Year 5: 13.12M, Year 6: 11.81M, Year 7: 10.63M, Year 8: 9.57M, Year 9: 8.61M, Year 10: 7.75M, Year 11: 4.58M (approximate); growth rate approximately -10% per year.

framework: Define decision criterion: choose the project with the higher NPV (positive profit), as there is no specific return threshold
Estimate revenues for each alternative: movies (probabilistic audience * ticket price * commission rate) and series (upfront + audience per episode * income per episode * number of episodes)
Estimate investment/costs for each alternative: sum all cost components; note sunk costs should be excluded
Calculate expected cash flows and apply NPV formula using 20% discount rate
Compare NPVs across alternatives; note that Movie alternative itself requires choosing between two director scenarios (Alt 1 vs Alt 2) with their own probabilities
Consider qualitative factors: competitive risk, production timing risk, economic environment, strategic fit
Assess additional revenue streams (merchandising, DVD/Blu-ray, games) and incorporate if data provided
Deliver a clear recommendation with key risks and suggested next steps

questions.prompt: Estimate the expected NPV for the Movie alternative (combining both director scenarios).
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a decision tree. For each director alternative, compute expected audience = (audience_good * prob_good) + (audience_bad * prob_bad). Then compute income = expected audience * ticket price * commission. Subtract investment to get cash flow, discount at 20% to get NPV. Then weight each alternative's NPV by its selection probability (60%/40%) to get overall movie NPV. A strong candidate will note that income is received at end of year 1 and investment at year 0.

math.setup: TA = (AudienceGood * %Good) + (AudienceBad * %Bad); Income = TA * $10/ticket * 10% commission; NPV = -Investment + Income / 1.20; Overall Movie NPV = NPV_Alt1 * 60% + NPV_Alt2 * 40%
math.answer: Expected NPV of Movie alternative = 260M USD

questions.prompt: Estimate the expected NPV for the Series alternative. What is the sunk cost trap here?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize that the script cost (10M USD, already paid) is a sunk cost and must NOT be included in the investment decision. Investment = 60M (actors) + 40M (production) = 100M USD, offset partially by 20M upfront, so net investment = 80M. Expected audience = sum of (audience_level * probability) * number of episodes. Income in year 1 = upfront (20M). Income in year 2 = total audience * income per episode. NPV = -80M + 20M/1.20 + 420M/1.20. A candidate who includes the sunk cost will get a lower (incorrect) NPV.

math.setup: TA = [(100M*30%)+(70M*40%)+(40M*30%)] * 10 episodes; Year 0 income = upfront 20M; Year 1 income = TA * 600,000 USD/episode; Net Investment = 100M - 20M upfront = 80M; NPV = -80 + 20/1.20 + 420/1.20
steps: Net investment at Year 0 = 100M - 20M = 80M (script 10M is sunk, excluded)
CF: Year 0 = -80M, Year 1 = +20M, Year 2 = +420M (but simplified: Year 0 = -80, Year 1 = 420 with upfront as Year 0 offset)
NPV = -80 + 20/1.20 + 420/1.20 = -80 + 16.67 + 350 = approximately 286.67M; casebook shows accumulated NPV = 270M using Year 1 income offset differently
Casebook simplified version: CF Year 0 = -80M, CF Year 1 = 420M; NPV = -80 + 350 = 270M USD (with upfront treated as Year 0 income reducing net investment)
math.answer: Series NPV = 270M USD (excluding sunk cost of 10M script). If candidate incorrectly includes sunk cost, NPV drops to approximately 260M USD.

questions.prompt: Comparing Movie NPV (260M) vs Series NPV (270M), which should the client choose? Would your answer change given Exhibit 3?
questions.guidance: Initial answer: Series has higher NPV (270M vs 260M), so recommend Series. Then Exhibit 3 introduces additional merchandising cash flows for Movie Alternative 2 (Bay). Candidate should identify the declining trend, calculate CAGR (-10%), and model as a growing perpetuity to add to Alternative 2's NPV. This changes the comparison.

math.setup: Growing perpetuity NPV = CF1 / (r - g); CF1 = 20M, g = -10% = -0.10, r = 20% = 0.20; New Alt 2 NPV = original Alt 2 NPV + perpetuity NPV; Recalculate overall movie NPV
steps: From Exhibit 3: initial cash flow = 20M USD, annual growth rate = -10%
Compare: Movie 287M vs Series 270M — Movie is now higher
math.answer: With merchandising cash flows, Movie NPV (287M) exceeds Series NPV (270M). The recommendation flips to choosing the Movie alternative.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential revenue streams and cost components for each alternative (movie vs series)?

categories.name: Series Revenue Streams
ideas: Viewer data value to streaming platform

recommendation: Initially recommend producing the Series (NPV 270M vs 260M for the Movie) given higher expected value before additional revenue streams are considered

However, once merchandising and ancillary cash flows from Movie Alternative 2 (Michael Bay) are factored in via a declining perpetuity (NPV 66.7M), the overall Movie NPV rises to 287M, which exceeds the Series NPV of 270M — recommend the Movie alternative

If selecting the Movie, the decision between directors depends on the company's audience strategy: Nolan targets Teenagers/Young Adults (60% selection probability, NPV 300M if chosen) versus Bay targeting Kids/Teenagers (40% selection probability, NPV 266.6M if chosen with merchandising)
risks: Significant uncertainty around audience reception and critic scores — actual outcomes may deviate sharply from probability estimates
Risk of not securing preferred director or talent within timeline
Production delays could cause the project to miss its target launch window
Competitor releases (a strong film in the same period) could cannibalize audience
Economic downturn reducing consumer discretionary spending on entertainment
Merchandising revenues are assumed in perpetuity with a stable -10% decay, which may not hold if the franchise loses relevance faster
next_steps: Conduct deeper market research on target audience preferences and competitive landscape
Negotiate talent contracts early to lock in Nolan or Bay before committing to the movie path
Develop contingency plans for production delays (buffer schedule, penalty clauses)
Stress-test the NPV model with downside scenarios (e.g., 50% reduction in audience)
Identify ways to reduce uncertainty, such as test screenings or pilot episodes for the series
Explore partnership structures with streaming platforms or studios to share risk
